Build an Ising Network

Source: R/estimate_network.R
build_ising.Rd

build_ising() estimates an Ising network for binary (0/1) variables: each variable is regressed on all the others with L1-penalised logistic regression, the penalty is chosen by EBIC, and the two estimates of each edge are combined into one undirected weight (van Borkulo et al., 2014). It is build_network() with method = "ising", and needs the glmnet package. The settings go in params: gamma (the EBIC hyperparameter, default 0.25), nlambda (default 100) and rule, "AND" (default: an edge only when both regressions select it) or "OR" (when either does).

An edge is a conditional association between two variables given all the others; an absent edge means the penalty removed it. Check the stability of the edges with bootstrap_network().

Usage

build_ising(data, actor = NULL, ...)

Arguments

data

The binary variables: a data frame with one row per observation and one column per variable, holding only 0 and 1. Non-numeric columns and a column named rid are set aside; columns with non-syntactic names, all-missing and constant columns, and rows with a missing value are dropped, each with a message; fewer than 2 variables or 3 complete rows, or any value other than 0 and 1, raise an error.

actor

An id column naming whose observation each row is; it is set aside, not modelled. Default NULL.

...

Further arguments for build_network(), such as params (gamma, nlambda, rule), threshold, scaling or group. method cannot be given: it is always "ising" (error of class nestimate_bad_input).

Value

A netobject (a netobject_group with group), exactly as build_network() returns it: print it for an overview, read the edges with extract_edges(), and draw it with cograph::splot().

References

van Borkulo, C. D., Borsboom, D., Epskamp, S., Blanken, T. F., Boschloo, L., Schoevers, R. A., & Waldorp, L. J. (2014). A new method for constructing networks from binary data. Scientific Reports, 4, 5918. doi:10.1038/srep05918

See also

build_network

Examples

if (requireNamespace("glmnet", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1)
  bin_data <- data.frame(matrix(rbinom(200, 1, 0.5), ncol = 5))
  net <- build_ising(bin_data)
}
